term: common through-source of all self-through bearers
definition: There exists c such that for every x, through w x x implies through w x c. c is the same candidate witness for all self-through bearers, not merely a common predicate. It is not asserted unique, actual or necessary by this definition. All self-through bearers are covered, including ones not assumed ultimate. No selfPowerFrom facts occur; this is a structural consequence of the two original power premises, not their identification.
note: Source-free premise-strength audit reusing the existing Context through relation. No source interpretation or independent adequacy claim is added. See docs/notes/necessary-simple-plurality.md, common-source strength audit.
